hook.line: Sometimes the news itself is the thing you want to react to, so you put it first and give your verdict after. It sounds a little more thought through than a quick comment.
hook.es: Que Altamira compre toda la cuadra nos parece injusto.
hook.en: The fact that Altamira is buying the whole block seems unfair to us.

examples.es: Que lo hayan despedido me parece injusto.
examples.en: The fact that they've fired him seems unfair to me.

examples.es: Que no te hayan avisado me parece increíble.
examples.en: The fact that they didn't tell you seems incredible to me.

examples.es: Que nadie haya dicho nada me parece raro.
examples.en: The fact that nobody has said anything seems strange to me.

examples.es: Que cierren el café me parece triste.
examples.en: The fact that they're closing the café seems sad to me.

examples.es: Que Altamira compre toda la cuadra nos parece injusto.
examples.en: The fact that Altamira is buying the whole block seems unfair to us.

examples.es: Que la empresa haya crecido tan rápido nos resulta sospechoso.
examples.en: The fact that the company has grown so fast strikes us as suspicious.

rule:
English starts with the fact that. Spanish starts with *que* and a subjunctive: *Que lo hayan despedido…* Then comes your verdict: *me parece injusto*.

The pieces:
*Que* + subjunctive (the news)
*me parece* / *nos parece* / *nos resulta* (who it seems to)
an adjective that stays masculine singular: *injusto*, *raro*, *triste*

The whole news item counts as one thing, so the verb is always *parece*, never *parecen*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a subject clause: the *que* part is the subject of *parece*.

It seems incredible to me that they didn't tell you.
I think they didn't tell you because it's incredible.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *me parece* or *me parecen* and type the whole sentence: *Que lo hayan despedido ___ injusto.* (The fact that they've fired him seems unfair to me.)
yourTurn.answer: Que lo hayan despedido me parece injusto.
yourTurn.why: The whole *que* part is one thing, so the verb is singular.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *me parece* or *nos parece* and type the whole sentence: *Que Altamira compre toda la cuadra ___ injusto.* (It seems unfair to us.)
yourTurn.answer: Que Altamira compre toda la cuadra nos parece injusto.
accept: Que Altamira compre toda la cuadra nos resulta injusto.
yourTurn.why: It seems that way to us, so *nos parece*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The fact that they didn't tell you seems incredible to me.
yourTurn.answer: Que no te hayan avisado me parece increíble.
yourTurn.why: A past event you're reacting to takes *hayan* plus the participle.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The fact that nobody has said anything seems strange to me.
yourTurn.answer: Que nadie haya dicho nada me parece raro.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The fact that they're closing the café seems sad to me.
yourTurn.answer: Que cierren el café me parece triste.
yourTurn.why: The news goes first, in the subjunctive, then your verdict.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, to a friend: It seems important to me that you come to the hearing.
yourTurn.answer: Que vengas a la audiencia me parece importante.

yourTurn.prompt: Change to *us*: *Que Vale haya llegado tarde me parece raro.*
yourTurn.answer: Que Vale haya llegado tarde nos parece raro.
accept: Que Vale haya llegado tarde nos resulta raro.

pitfalls.wrong: Que lo han despedido me parece injusto.
pitfalls.right: Que lo hayan despedido me parece injusto.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You're judging the news, not just reporting it, so the verb after *que* is subjunctive.

pitfalls.wrong: Que cierren el café me parece tristemente.
pitfalls.right: Que cierren el café me parece triste.
pitfalls.why: After *parece* Spanish uses an adjective, like English seems sad, not an adverb.

pitfalls.wrong: Lo hayan despedido me parece injusto.
pitfalls.right: Que lo hayan despedido me parece injusto.
pitfalls.why: The *que* is what opens the fact, like the fact that in English, so it has to stay.

personal: Think of a piece of news that bothers you or pleases you. Write it as *Que… me parece…* with a subjunctive and an adjective.
